_comment: Functions that will never be matched by writing C, because they were not
produced by a C compiler. They are excluded from the work queue: without
this the scheduler keeps offering them, and they look like ideal targets
-- tiny, high fan-in, adjacent to easy matches. A wave-5 agent spent its
budget proving out this list, which is the only reason it exists.
Adding to this list is a claim that needs evidence in the reason field.
'I could not match it' is not evidence; the tells are in the
Cheap pre-filter when scoping a new batch:

functions.sub_0802C62A: Not code at all -- inter-function alignment padding. sub_0802C604 ends `bx r1` at 0x0802C628, and the two bytes at 0x0802C62A are the 0x0000 the assembler emits for `.align 2, 0` ahead of the 4-aligned sub_0802C62C. `movs r0, r0` is simply how 0x0000 disassembles. Zero callers.
functions.sub_0806F734: Hand-rolled mode switch (`add r2, pc, #0; bx r2`) at the head of the m4a/MP2K sound driver. Hand-written, not linker-generated.
functions.sub_0806F9A4: ARM code cut out as a THUMB unit. It sits between ARM instructions using r8/lr and `arm_func_start sub_0806F9AC`; the ARM stream above branches straight over it with `bgt sub_0806F9AC`. Its two halfwords are one ARM word. Note the usual grep does NOT catch this one -- it is a word-aligned `thumb_func_start`, not `non_word_aligned`; what gives it away is an `arm_func_start` immediately below and a body that reads registers it never sets and never returns.
functions.sub_0806F9A8: ARM code cut out as a THUMB unit, same as sub_0806F9A4 directly above it. Body is `movs r0, #4; lsls r0, r4, #0xe`, which reads r4 without setting it and has no `bx`. Reassembled as one ARM word, 0x03A02004 is `moveq r2, #4` -- what the m4a mixer actually executes.
functions.sub_0806FB66: m4a/MP2K sound driver. Not a function: a `bx r3` tail plus a literal pool, and the pool word is 0x68736D53 = "Smsh", the m4a ID_NUMBER that its apparent caller sub_0806F744 compares against. Same shape as sub_0807003C.
functions.sub_0806FC08: m4a/MP2K sound driver, hand-written assembly. It is a single `ldr r2, [r1, #0x40]` that falls through into non_word_aligned_thumb_func_start sub_0806FC0A, and BOTH are bl targets -- two callable entry points two bytes apart in one instruction stream. See also sub_0806F740, a raw `.hword 0xFF1E` the disassembler could not decode.
functions.sub_0807003C: m4a/MP2K sound driver. Not a function at all: the `bx r3` tail of the routine above it plus a literal pool. The split drew a unit boundary mid-function.
functions.sub_0807031C: m4a/MP2K sound driver, hand-written assembly. Returns its result in r3 rather than r0, which no agbcc output does.
functions.sub_080718E8: Linker THUMB->ARM interworking veneer: `bx pc; nop` plus an arm_func_start holding `b sub_08000304`. The 4-byte unit the index reports is only the THUMB half of an 8-byte veneer, cut at the mode change. The linker synthesises these when a THUMB bl targets an ARM symbol; no C construct emits one.
functions.sub_080718F0: Linker THUMB->ARM interworking veneer, branches to sub_08000234.
